cat > forgemyspec-bundle/csv-dedup/spec.yaml <<'E'
version: "0.1"
title: "CSV deduplicator CLI"
objective: "Provide data_dedup.py, a stdlib-only single-file Python CLI that removes duplicate CSV rows by a composite key using keep-first, keep-last or error strategies, writes an output CSV and prints a summary."
execution_mode: critical
context:
  system: "Empty Python repository; single module data_dedup.py at the repository root, unittest tests under tests/."
  assumptions:
    - "The input CSV has a header row; key columns are selected by header name."
    - "Rows are compared by exact string equality of the key column values (no trimming or case folding)."
    - "Input and output are UTF-8 with csv module default dialect handling; output keeps the input header and column order."
    - "Surviving rows keep their original relative order; with keep-last the survivor sits at the position of the last occurrence."
    - "A duplicate is any row beyond the first sharing a key; found count equals rows minus distinct keys."
constraints:
  - "Python standard library only; no third-party packages."
  - "All code lives in the single file data_dedup.py."
  - "No fuzzy matching, no whole-file in-place editing, no formats other than CSV."
  - "In error strategy no output file is written."
success_criteria:
  - "Composite keys of one or more columns dedupe correctly under first, last and error strategies."
  - "Error strategy exits non-zero and lists the duplicate keys with row numbers."
  - "Summary prints duplicates found and removed."
hypotheses:
  - {id: h1, description: "Rows sharing the same values in all key columns are treated as duplicates, and rows differing in any key column are kept.", confidence: 0.9}
  - {id: h2, description: "Strategy first keeps the earliest occurrence and strategy last keeps the latest occurrence, preserving order of survivors.", confidence: 0.9}
  - {id: h3, description: "Strategy error exits non-zero, reports each duplicate key with row numbers, and writes no output when duplicates exist.", confidence: 0.85}
  - {id: h4, description: "The output CSV has the input header and only the surviving rows, and the summary prints the number of duplicates found and removed.", confidence: 0.9}
  - {id: h5, description: "A missing key column or unreadable input exits non-zero with a clear message naming the problem.", confidence: 0.85}
required_evidence:
  - "unittest run output of tests/ with all tests passing"
  - "forgemyspec gate report showing RESULT: PASS"
actions:
  - {id: a1, description: "Implement data_dedup.py CLI with argparse, dedupe core and summary", type: implement, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h1, h2, h3, h4, h5]}
  - {id: a2, description: "Write unittest boundary tests for each obligation", type: implement, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h1, h2, h3, h4, h5]}
  - {id: a3, description: "Run the gate and review the report", type: validate, requires_confirmation: false, supports: [h1, h2, h3, h4, h5]}
decision_rules:
  - "If a behavior is not covered by an obligation, stop and request a spec amendment."
  - "If the gate fails, fix the implementation, never the tests or the spec."
metadata:
  source_prompt: "Build a CSV deduplicator CLI in Python. Remove duplicate rows by a key made of one or more columns (composite keys), with three strategies: keep first, keep last, or error (exit non-zero and report duplicates). Write the result to an output CSV and print a summary of how many duplicates were found and removed. Single file data_dedup.py, stdlib only."
  generator: claude-code-session
  scope_contract:
    must_include:
      - "composite key"
      - "keep first"
      - "keep last"
      - "error strategy exits non-zero"
      - "output CSV"
      - "summary of duplicates found and removed"
      - "single file data_dedup.py"
      - "stdlib only"
      - "missing column reported"
formal:
  module: DataDedup
  obligations:
    - id: composite_key
      kind: boundary
      statement: "Rows are duplicates only if all key columns match; rows differing in any key column are kept."
      hypotheses: [h1]
      must_include: ["composite key"]
      test: "test_data_dedup.DedupTests.test_composite_key"
    - id: keep_first
      kind: boundary
      statement: "Strategy first keeps the earliest row of each key, in original order."
      hypotheses: [h2]
      must_include: ["keep first"]
      test: "test_data_dedup.DedupTests.test_keep_first"
    - id: keep_last
      kind: boundary
      statement: "Strategy last keeps the latest row of each key, ordered by position of that row."
      hypotheses: [h2]
      must_include: ["keep last"]
      test: "test_data_dedup.DedupTests.test_keep_last"
    - id: error_strategy
      kind: boundary
      statement: "Strategy error with duplicates exits non-zero, reports duplicate keys with row numbers, and writes no output file."
      hypotheses: [h3]
      must_include: ["error strategy exits non-zero"]
      test: "test_data_dedup.DedupTests.test_error_strategy_exits_nonzero"
    - id: output_csv
      kind: boundary
      statement: "The output CSV contains the input header followed by the surviving rows."
      hypotheses: [h4]
      must_include: ["output CSV"]
      test: "test_data_dedup.DedupTests.test_output_csv"
    - id: summary
      kind: boundary
      statement: "The CLI prints the number of duplicates found and removed (error strategy: found, removed 0)."
      hypotheses: [h4]
      must_include: ["summary of duplicates found and removed"]
      test: "test_data_dedup.DedupTests.test_summary"
    - id: missing_column
      kind: boundary
      statement: "A key column absent from the header exits non-zero and names the missing column; a missing input file also exits non-zero."
      hypotheses: [h5]
      must_include: ["missing column reported"]
      test: "test_data_dedup.DedupTests.test_missing_column"
    - id: single_file_stdlib
      kind: boundary
      statement: "data_dedup.py is one file and imports only standard library modules."
      hypotheses: [h4]
      must_include: ["single file data_dedup.py", "stdlib only"]
      test: "test_data_dedup.DedupTests.test_stdlib_only"
scope:
  paths: ["data_dedup.py", "tests/**"]
  tests: tests
  pythonpath: ["."]
E
export PYTHONPATH=.forgemyspec/harness
python3 -m forgemyspec lint forgemyspec-bundle/csv-dedup/spec.yaml --formal && python3 -m forgemyspec package forgemyspec-bundle/csv-dedup/spec.yaml && python3 -m forgemyspec board start R1; python3 -m forgemyspec board

**Spec:** `forgemyspec-bundle/csv-dedup/spec.yaml` is a spec-only bundle with boundary tests and no Dafny contract. It covers `data_dedup.py` and `tests/**`.

**What approving locks in:**
- **Key:** columns are chosen by header name, and one or more can be combined into a composite key. Values are compared as exact strings, with no trimming or case folding.
- **Strategies:** `first` keeps the earliest row for each key. `last` keeps the latest row, placed at the position of that last occurrence. Surviving rows keep their original order.
- **Error strategy:** with duplicates, it exits non-zero and lists each duplicate key with its row numbers. It writes no output file.
- **Output and summary:** the output CSV has the input header followed by the surviving rows. The summary prints how many duplicates were found and removed. With the error strategy that is "found N, removed 0".
- **Bad input:** a key column missing from the header, or a missing input file, exits non-zero and names the problem.
- **Constraints:** one file, `data_dedup.py`, using only the standard library.
